questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Social Responsibility' refers to.
questions.a: Social responsibility of business refers to the obligation of business enterprises to act in ways that protect and promote the interests of all stakeholders -- owners, employees, consumers, government, and the community -- while pursuing economic objectives.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Social Responsibility'.
questions.a: Social responsibility means businesses must balance profit-making with their duties towards all stakeholders and society at large, not just shareholders.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Social Responsibility' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Social Responsibility: Concept and Meaning

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Arguments for Social Responsibility' refers to.
questions.a: Arguments for social responsibility include long-run business interest, better public image, avoidance of government regulation, moral justification, resource availability, and contribution to solving social problems created by business.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Arguments for Social Responsibility'.
questions.a: Being socially responsible benefits business in the long run by building trust, avoiding regulation, and justifying the use of societal resources.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Arguments for Social Responsibility' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Arguments for Social Responsibility

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Arguments Against Social Responsibility' refers to.
questions.a: Arguments against social responsibility include the view that business exists for profit, that social responsibility dilutes business goals, that it lacks accountability, that it involves high cost, and that business lacks social expertise to solve social problems.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Arguments Against Social Responsibility'.
questions.a: Critics argue that business should focus on profit, that social responsibility lacks accountability and expertise, and that it imposes costs that reduce efficiency.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Arguments Against Social Responsibility' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Arguments Against Social Responsibility

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Business Ethics' refers to.
questions.a: Business ethics refers to the moral principles and standards that guide the conduct of business, determining what is right or wrong in business decisions and actions, and covering issues like fair trade, honest advertising, and ethical treatment of stakeholders.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Business Ethics'.
questions.a: Business ethics are the moral principles that guide business conduct, ensuring decisions are not only legal and profitable but also morally right.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Business Ethics' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Business Ethics

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Elements of Business Ethics' refers to.
questions.a: The key elements of business ethics include top management commitment, publication of a code of conduct, establishment of compliance mechanisms, involvement of employees at all levels, and measurement of results to ensure ethical practices are followed.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Elements of Business Ethics'.
questions.a: Effective business ethics require leadership commitment, a clear code of conduct, compliance mechanisms, employee involvement, and ongoing measurement of ethical performance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Elements of Business Ethics' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Elements of Business Ethics

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Social Responsibility Towards Different Groups' refers to.
questions.a: Business has social responsibility towards different stakeholder groups: shareholders (fair return), employees (fair wages and safety), consumers (quality and fair price), community (environment and development), and government (taxes and compliance).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Social Responsibility Towards Different Groups'.
questions.a: A socially responsible business must discharge its duties towards all stakeholder groups -- shareholders, employees, consumers, community, and government -- in a balanced manner.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Social Responsibility Towards Different Groups' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Social Responsibility Towards Different Interest Groups

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Social Responsibility Towards Consumers' refers to.
questions.a: Business responsibility towards consumers includes providing quality goods and services at fair prices, honest advertising, after-sales service, safe products, and redressal of consumer grievances, as consumers are often vulnerable to exploitation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Social Responsibility Towards Consumers'.
questions.a: Consumers are the most vulnerable stakeholder group, so businesses must ensure quality, fair pricing, honest information, and grievance redressal to protect their interests.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Social Responsibility Towards Consumers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Responsibility Towards Consumers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Corporate Governance' refers to.
questions.a: Corporate governance is the system of rules, practices, and processes by which a company is directed and controlled, ensuring transparency, accountability, and fairness in its relationship with all stakeholders, particularly shareholders and management.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Corporate Governance'.
questions.a: Corporate governance ensures that companies are managed in a transparent and accountable manner, balancing the interests of shareholders, management, and other stakeholders.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Corporate Governance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Corporate Governance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'CSR in India' refers to.
questions.a: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in India refers to the statutory and voluntary initiatives by companies to integrate social and environmental concerns in their operations, with the Companies Act mandating qualifying companies to spend a portion of profits on CSR activities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'CSR in India'.
questions.a: CSR in India combines voluntary social initiatives with statutory requirements, requiring qualifying companies to spend a specified percentage of profits on socially beneficial activities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'CSR in India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Corporate Social Responsibility in India
